description: News 2023-2026 on memory fab capacity additions (Samsung P4/P5, SK hynix M15X/Yongin, Micron Idaho/Hiroshima, CXMT), wafer capacity numbers, capex, and reported production/wafer-input cuts by Korean makers.

rows.value_or_summary: Cutting wafer input for legacy DDR4 and 128-layer NAND since Apr 2023; DRAM cut to continue at least to end-2023, output increase expected H2 2024

rows.item: DDR4 share of DRAM output cut
rows.value_or_summary: DDR4 to fall to ~20% of DRAM output by end-2024 (from 40% end-Jun, 30% end-Sep 2024), citing CXMT legacy supply
Said on earnings call it would reduce general DRAM and NAND output to match weaker demand; no % given
Samsung/SK hynix trimmed legacy NAND output; Micron began cutting NAND wafer input; 1Q25 NAND contract prices seen -10~15%
Cut >10%: ~200k to ~170k wafers/month; Hwaseong lines 12 and 17 also adjusted down
1.9m wafers (2025) -> 1.7m (2026), about -10%; capacity tilted to DRAM/HBM
Target ~200k wafers/month of 1c DRAM by end-2026 (~60k end-2025, +80k by 2Q26, +60k in 4Q26); total DRAM capacity est. 650-700k wpm
Construction resumed after 2-year pause; targeted operation 2028 for HBM and 1c DRAM

P4 recently operational with 1c DRAM line for HBM; P5 final completion targeted 2030, possible triple-fab (>1.5x P4 capacity) pending approval; KRW 6tn Onyang HBM fab groundbreaking Sep 2026; Hwaseong H1 idle cleanroom used for general DRAM; large new supply seen limited before 2028
Equipment move-in Nov 2025, inauguration 4Q25; initial 1b DRAM target ~10k wafers/month for HBM
Opening moved ~3 months earlier to Feb 2027; no official capacity figure

rows.item: DRAM wafer capacity now and 2030 target (reported)
rows.value_or_summary: ~550k DRAM wpm now (incl. ~200k Wuxi); target ~1m wpm by 2030-31; M15X ~40k wpm from 2H26 -> ~80k in 2027; Yongin fab 1 to add ~360k wpm by 1H30; new capacity all DRAM

rows.item: Fab timelines and capex per US IPO prospectus
rows.value_or_summary: M15X cleanroom opened Oct 2025, wafer input from 1Q26; Yongin phase-1 cleanroom 1Q27; P&T7 packaging end-2027; Indiana packaging 2H28. PP&E cash capex: W8.3tn (2023), W15.9tn (2024), W27.5tn (2025); 2026 to rise considerably
Idaho ID1 DRAM wafer output to begin 2H 2027; ID2 before first New York fab; NY groundbreaking slipped to late 2025; Hiroshima next-gen DRAM mass production targeted 2026 (EUV); $200bn US plan
Net capex $27.37bn (gross $30.71bn); FQ4-26 net $10.77bn
FQ1-27 capex ~ $11.5bn; 1H FY27 ~ $25bn, higher again in 2H; opex +~$2.5bn; supply-demand seen tighter in FY27-28 than FY26 (wording per headline feed, garbled)

DRAM capex $53.7bn (2025) -> $61.3bn (2026, +14%); NAND $21.1bn -> $22.2bn (+5%); SK hynix $20.5bn (+17%), Samsung $20bn (+11%), Micron $13.5bn (+23%); limited bit-output effect in 2026, cleanroom-constrained; ID1 not before 2027
~100k wpm at start of 2024 -> ~290k wpm by end-2025 (via Communications Today); UBS sees China memory capacity +120-140k wpm in 2026
~300k wpm across 2 Hefei + 1 Beijing fabs; ~350k wpm by end-2026 (vs Micron ~375k); >600k wpm once Shanghai/Hefei expansions complete (no date); considering 2nd Beijing fab
Shanghai STAR listing raising ~CNY 57.9bn (~$8.6bn) for next-gen process, HBM3 development and capacity

notes: Most capacity numbers are press/analyst reports (TrendForce citing Korean media, Omdia) rather than company disclosures; companies rarely publish wafers/month. Two 2023 rows included for context on the last Korean cut. No reported Korean DRAM wafer-input cuts in 2025-2026 were found; cuts in 2024-2026 concerned legacy DDR4 and NAND. No reliable DRAM fab utilization-rate percentages for Samsung/SK hynix in 2024-2026 were found -> omitted. Micron FY27 capex: only headline-feed summary found (prepared remarks not fetched); SK hynix 2Q26 / Samsung 2Q26 call capacity comments not captured. Micron Hiroshima 2026 ramp status not confirmed beyond the 2025 plan.
